title: When Can I Sleep Without a Bra After Breast Augmentation?
meta_description: Not in the first 3 to 4 weeks: university handouts keep a support bra on 24 hours a day. No source dates going braless, so your surgeon clears you.
excerpt: A support bra stays on day and night for the first 3 to 4 weeks, according to university handouts. No medical source gives a date for going braless at night, so your surgeon clears you. Here is how long each bra stage lasts, what to wear to bed, and what can delay it.
quick_answer:
When can I sleep without a bra after breast augmentation?

Once your surgeon clears you, and not in the first 3 to 4 weeks: UW Medicine and University of Utah Health keep a surgical bra on 24 hours a day for that long. No medical source we read gives a date for going braless at night. Underwire waits until your incisions are fully healed.

images.text_in_image:
Bra Stages After Breast Augmentation
Surgical or support bra: 24 hours a day for 3 to 4 weeks. Off only to shower.
Soft, supportive sports bra: After 3 to 4 weeks.
No bra at night: No source gives a date. Your surgeon clears you.
Underwire bra: Not until incisions are fully healed.
Sources: UW Medicine; University of Utah Health. Follow your surgeon's plan.

sources.title: Breast Augmentation: What to expect and how to prepare
quotes: Your doctor will decide if you need a surgical bra. If you are given one, keep it on 24 hours a day for 3 to 4 weeks. Take it off only when you shower.
If your doctor decides you do not need a surgical bra, you can still wear one. Or, wear what is comfortable.
Do not wear an underwire bra until your incisions are fully healed.
Sleep on your back for the first 3 to 4 weeks, whether or not you are wearing a surgical bra. After that, you may sleep on your side or stomach.
A fever higher than 100.5°F (38°C)
Bad-smelling drainage

sources.title: Recovering from Breast Reduction & Breast Augmentation
quotes: You will wear a surgical bra for three to four weeks after your surgery. You should only remove the bra to shower or to wash it.
In the beginning, it’s also best to wear shirts that are easy to put on and take off, such as loose button-down shirts or zip-up hoodies.
After three to four weeks of wearing the surgical bra, you can transition into a soft, supportive sports bra.
For the first week after surgery, you should rest and sleep on your back, with extra pillows to prop you up. This can help with swelling.
Do not sleep on your stomach until your surgeon says it’s okay.
a limited range of motion in your shoulders, which may require someone to help you with certain tasks like putting on clothes,
You may feel shooting pains, tingling, or other strange sensations in your skin for the first few months.
You may experience some asymmetry since each breast may heal at a different rate.

sources.title: Cosmetic breast surgery - discharge
quotes: Once you no longer need dressings, wear a soft, wireless, supportive bra night and day for 2 to 4 weeks.
Smoking slows healing and increases your risk for complications and infection.

sources.title: What should I expect during my breast augmentation recovery?
quotes: Wear your support garment (a bra or elastic band, called a bandeau) around the clock as instructed by your plastic surgeon.
an elastic bandage or support bra will minimize swelling and support the breasts as they heal.

sources.title: Breast Augmentation - Aftercare & Recovery
quotes: Rest and sleep on your back in an inclined position (25-to 45-degree angle) for the initial postoperative days or if you have significant swelling. Use wedge pillows with an incline design or sleep in a recliner chair.
Most residual swelling will resolve within a month.
Your breasts may feel tight and sensitive to the touch
